hypothesis: Blind geothermal feeder faults in the Great Basin that lack mapped surface scarps in existing_faults.tif are uniquely fingerprinted by the spatial conjunction of (1) deep-to-surface geothermometer disequilibrium (T_quartz - T_chalcedony, T_cation - T_quartz) and flash/conductive cooling surplus (max(T_quartz, T_cation) - T_discharge) back-projected up-dip to basement steps, (2) elevation- and playa-detrended electrical conductivity clay-cap edges concordant with magnetite-destructive RTP troughs, (3) sentinel-cleaned microseismic density coupled with transtensional shear-dilatation rate, and (4) 4-modality spin-2 axial strike coherence paired with 1 m LiDAR micro-scarp strike concordance. Pooling these 12 zero-catalogue channels (GCSD-12) with the cached 44 physics + 12 TDKL + 12 VESS stack via a Tri-Specialist Log-Odds Product-of-Experts (PoE) architecture improves whole-fault recovery over H88-ADHR (0.190436), H88-TDKL (0.196237), and H88-VESS (0.200941), while a 4-quadrant out-of-fold (OOF) Three-Stratum Axial-Crest Dinkelbach allocator resolves the IR-88-112 near-ribbon 3-px dot overlap against all ~270 registry and concurrent rasters.
mechanism: gdr_wellspring_in_footprint.csv (T_qtz, T_chalc, T_cat, T_surf) + 2m_temperature_probe + paleo_geothermal + training_features.tif B2/B3/B4/B6/B7/B8/B9/B10/B11/B12/B13/B15/B16/B17/B18/B19 + lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif B4/B5/B8/B9/B10/B11/B12 -> 12 label-blind GCSD channels (src/gems88/gcsd.py) -> Tri-Specialist dual-expectation HGB ensemble (base 44/67ch + geomorphic-vesselness 68/91ch + hydrothermal-seismic-strike 80/103ch) -> Log-Odds PoE with blind-basin tail preservation -> Bayesian completeness fusion -> 4-quadrant OOF Three-Stratum Axial-Crest Dinkelbach allocation (relay 2<d<=9px, piedmont 9<d<=25px, blind basin d>25px; share_gt25>=0.40, share_le2==0.0)
named_non_fault_mimic: Closed-basin evaporite playa brines and lateral shallow groundwater outflow plumes on flat valley floors (high electrical conductivity and distal warm wells displaced down-gradient from the range-front feeder fault), circular volcanic plug edifices, and Pleistocene Lake Lahontan/Bonneville highstand strandlines (1330 m and 1555 m contours). Mitigated via up-dip basement-step back-projection, local elevation/playa detrending of conductivity, 1 m LiDAR-to-crustal strike alignment, and an explicit playa/volcanic/shoreline mimic penalty channel.
